steps.title: Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have your joints felt since you finished care with us? I usually hear one of three things. Still feeling good, some pain returning, or pretty much back to where you started. Which one is closest for you?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Still Feeling Good
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. Your notes say we helped with {{complaint_reference}}. Is it nice to move without that pain getting in the way?

(Let them answer.)

steps.title: Pain Starting to Return
steps.content:
I'm sorry to hear that, {{contact_first_name}}. Joint pain can return after care ends. Your notes say you had made good progress. What do you think brought it back?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Pain Fully Back
steps.content:
I'm sorry to hear that, {{contact_first_name}}. Joint pain can return after care ends. Your notes say you had made good progress. Was there a new injury, or did it return slowly?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm updating your file while we talk. Can I ask a few questions about your joints?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, we'll come back to {{complaint_reference}}. First, can I ask a few joint questions so your file is current?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Joint Questions
steps.content:
(Write down every concern they name.)

Is either knee bothering you?

How about either hip?

Is either shoulder bothering you?

Any trouble with your hands or grip?

Any neck or back pain?

Any morning stiffness?

Any swelling after activity?

Are you taking any medications for joint pain?

Of those, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Joint Questions
steps.content:
(Write down every concern they name.)

Is either knee bothering you?

How about either hip?

Is either shoulder bothering you?

Any trouble with your hands or grip?

Any neck or back pain?

Any morning stiffness?

Any swelling after activity?

Are you taking any medications for joint pain?

Between these and what returned, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Understand the Concern
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask about {{main_concern}} so your file is current.

(Ask these three questions in order. Pause after each.)

How long has that been bothering you?

(Let them answer.)

Is it happening here and there, or most days?

(Let them answer.)

How does it affect your day or the things you enjoy?

(Let them open up. Do not rush.)

Thank you for sharing that. It makes sense.

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in so {{provider_name}} can take a look at {{main_concern}}. If we can help, we'll explain your options. If not, we'll tell you that too. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you said {{main_concern}} has been bothering you. I don't want to assume anything. Is it timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Let them answer. Do not argue.)

steps.title: Why Did They Stop?
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad your joints are still feeling good.

Can I ask what changed that led you to stop coming in for check-ins?

(Let them answer. Do not argue.)

(Tap the reason they shared.)

steps.title: Objection: Pain Returned
steps.content:
That can happen after care stops. A visit lets us see what's changed and talk through your options.

Can we get you in for that look?

steps.title: Objection: Getting Older
steps.content:
Getting older does not mean you have to ignore joint pain. We can look at what's happening and discuss what may help.

Would you be open to that?

steps.title: Objection: Pain Relievers
steps.content:
I understand. Pain relievers may help for a while. A visit lets us look at the joint itself.

Can we at least take a look?

steps.title: Reason: Feeling Fine
steps.content:
That makes sense, {{contact_first_name}}. When your joints feel good, coming in stops feeling urgent. Check-ins help us notice changes before they disrupt your routine.

Does that sound right?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap it. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get a joint check-in on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Reason: Cost or Insurance
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. You're not committing to treatment. The first step is a visit to check how your joints are doing.

Does that seem fair?

(Let them answer.)

(Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap it. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get that joint check-in scheduled. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Reason: Life Got Busy
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Life fills up fast, and check-ins get pushed down the list. We can find a time that works around your schedule.

Would that help?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap it. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's find an easy time for a joint check-in. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Reason: Waiting for Pain
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Joint changes can begin before they interfere with your day. A check-in lets us see how things are holding up.

Would a quick check-in work?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap it. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get a joint check-in on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Reason: Moved or Switched
steps.content:
That's understandable, {{contact_first_name}}. Things change. If you're nearby, your joint care history is still in your file here.

Would you like us to take another look?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap it. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get a joint check-in on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

Are you taking any medications for joint pain?

Between these and the pain that's back, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Objection: Needs Time
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. What part would you like to think over?

(Listen. Tap the matching reason if they name one.)

A visit gives you information about {{main_concern}}. Then you can decide what feels right.

Does that help?

steps.title: Objection: Send Information
steps.content:
I'd be glad to send information, {{contact_first_name}}. General information cannot show what's happening with {{main_concern}}. A visit gives us a chance to look at it.

Could we schedule the visit first?
